newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian premier confident on CEFTA membership.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian premier confident on CEFTA membership.

text.p: Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said on Friday he was confident Bulgaria would soon join the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) following the signing of bilateral accords with several member states.

"Bulgaria has the chance to be accepted into CEFTA in the near future because we have concluded free trade agreements this year with the Czech Republic and Slovakia," the state news agency BTA quoted him as saying.

Videnov, who later left for Slovakia to attend a summit of CEFTA prime ministers, said Bulgaria was also hoping to clinch free trade accords with the other member states -- Poland, Hungary and Slovenia and with aspiring member Romania.
"Joining CEFTA will be an important step towards Bulgaria's integration into a united Europe and towards our full membership of the World Trade Organisation," he added.
Trade minister Atanas Paparizov accompanied Videnov to Slovakia, which holds CEFTA's annually rotating chairmanship.
Earlier on Friday Slovak officials said Romania was expected to join the trade bloc next year. CEFTA was formed in 1992 to replace the communist-era trading bloc Comecon.
